## Collections and measurements

The table summarises stool collections with linked metagenomic and metabolomic measurements, consistent responses to four dietary questions and a recorded antibiotic flag. Participants can contribute multiple collections. Exact external assay identifiers and unique documentary collection matches are tabulated separately. [Data sources and linkage](../docs/DATA.md)

```{r reconstruction, echo=FALSE}
counts <- read.csv("../results/tables/reference_counts.csv", stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
labels <- c(
  collections = "Linked collections",
  participants = "Participants",
  crohn_participants = "Participants with Crohn’s disease",
  non_ibd_participants = "Participants without IBD",
  crohn_collections = "Collections from participants with Crohn’s disease",
  non_ibd_collections = "Collections from participants without IBD",
  participants_with_repeat_collections = "Participants with repeated collections",
  exact_id_pairs = "Exact external assay ID matches",
  documentary_collection_pairs = "Unique collection-key matches",
  microbiome_genera = "Genus-level taxonomic entries",
  metabolomic_peaks = "Metabolomic peaks",
  microbiome_all_zero = "All-zero microbial profiles",
  metabolome_all_zero = "All-zero metabolomic profiles"
)
stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(counts$metric), setequal(counts$metric, names(labels)))
table <- data.frame(Measure = unname(labels[counts$metric]), Count = counts$value)
knitr::kable(table, format = "pipe")
```

## Relation to the dietary analyses

The primary analysis compares intervals within people with Crohn’s disease using metagenomes and whole-grain reports. The wider dietary analysis additionally requires complete dietary recall, and the butyrate comparison uses visits with metabolomic measurements. These eligibility rules give each analysis its own denominator. [Statistical analysis plan](../docs/HMP2-analysis-plan.md)
